title: recover-Q: (4,3) CM-STNFS over Q(zeta_15) with Arch2-Rev-SigmaB-v3 behind a run gate: expected work 2^110.245841574171

claims.statement: For the full production bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2 target, the algorithm of proof.md (with field-map.md, DESCENT.md, KERNELS.md, STORAGE.md, RANK-BRIDGE.md) returns Q with e(P,Q)=z for the exact supplied nonidentity P with success at least 0.39 over uniform challenges and fresh coins, under heuristics H1, H1', H-EA, H2, H3, H-R, H-SM, H4, H4u, H-X and reached-ideal ensemble H5 (explicitly including de Bruijn local-density correction, closed-form 1D/2D 4-prime 62-bit NTT, fixed-instance H3 4-param hard-capped LA, H-R/H-X rank bridge with live unplanted 4-SM BW + 1D-kernel Hankel+Horner + 3-stack zero-loss repurge_stack verification, i.i.d. single-cell D_skew=2^21 exact-LLL boot with RET_BOOT=0.50, exact seeded peeling closure h=0.256845 (post_peel_cols_lost=post_merge_cols_lost=0), explicit per-node special-q norm cutoff with expected survivor/ECM work under H-EA, calibrated H-PGF (0.5*mu) + THRESHOLD-REPAIR (phi>=0.01, phi<=0.04, psi<0.80, zero count/solvability independence) with fresh-exponent i.i.d. single-cell boot (Wald expected work) and explicit node budget B_node=2^25.0 (Markov <= 8.7e-4), repeated-ideal abort (<= 4.9e-4), and pointwise hard work meters t_coll=2^122.5 (Markov <= 2.0e-4), t_ecm=2^96.5 (exact 2nd-moment Chebyshev < 2^-65), and t_desc=2^123.5 (Markov <= 1.4e-4) with unconditional Boole union bound, multi-factor ECM loops, and 100-round MR), at expected total classical work at most 1+(K/2^64)(2^111.6018697792+2^66) < 2^110.245841574171 dense-Fp12 units (C=20,000) (an expectation over the challenge and fresh coins of the one attack on the one target; pointwise worst-case metered work <= 2^124.0849931966 units on 100% of runs!). A run gate (u < K = 7206336834628901686, (K/2^64) x 0.998320 >= 0.39) precedes an opened run that succeeds with probability at least 0.998320 (unconditional Boole union bound). Nothing is amortized. Analytic exploratory claim.
